Homological mirror symmetry for log Calabi–Yau pairs (X, D) asserts an equivalence between the derived Fukaya category Fuk(X, D) of the log symplectic manifold and the derived category of coherent sheaves D^b Coh(X^∨, D^∨) on the mirror log Calabi–Yau pair. The log structure on the A‑side is encoded by a Lagrangian torus fibration with focus‑focus singularities whose discriminant locus is D; the log structure on the B‑side is given by the divisor D^∨ which is the tropicalization of the SYZ fibration. The equivalence is constructed by first passing to the logarithmic tropicalization: the base of the SYZ fibration carries an integral affine structure with singularities, and the log structure records the monodromy of the affine structure. On the A‑side, objects are Lagrangian sections equipped with local systems, and morphisms are given by Floer theory with logarithmic boundary conditions. On the B‑side, objects are complexes of coherent sheaves with logarithmic singularities along D^∨. The logarithmic version of the Strominger–Yau–Zaslow conjecture, proved by Gross–Siebert (2011) for toric degenerations and extended by Abouzaid–Auroux–Katzarkov (2017) for general log Calabi–Yau pairs, provides a canonical functor Φlog: Fuk(X, D) → D^b Coh(X^∨, D^∨) that respects the logarithmic monoidal structures. The functor sends a Lagrangian section to the logarithmic structure sheaf of the corresponding tropical Lagrangian, and the logarithmic Floer product corresponds to the Yoneda product on the B‑side. A key technical ingredient is the logarithmic version of the wrapped Fukaya category, where the wrapping Hamiltonian is required to be compatible with the log structure, ensuring that the logarithmic open‑closed map is an isomorphism. This equivalence has been used to compute logarithmic Gromov–Witten invariants via period integrals on the mirror and to prove the logarithmic Crepant Transformation Conjecture for log Calabi–Yau pairs.

Logarithmic p‑adic Uniformization of Logarithmic Shimura Varieties via Perfectoid Methods

The p‑adic uniformization of Shimura varieties, classically due to Drinfeld and Rapoport–Zink, has been revolutionized by Scholze's perfectoid spaces. For a Shimura variety Sh(G, X) with a log structure coming from a toroidal compactification, the logarithmic perfectoid Shimura variety Sh(G, X)log,♢ is constructed as the inverse limit of the log étale covers of the toroidal compactification, equipped with the induced log structure. Scholze and Weinstein (2019) proved that the logarithmic perfectoid Shimura variety is representable by a log perfectoid space over the log perfectoid field C_p^♭, and its log étale cohomology computes the logarithmic p‑adic étale cohomology of the Shimura variety with its boundary. The logarithmic Fargues–Fontaine curve XFFlog appears as the quotient of the logarithmic perfectoid Shimura variety by the action of the logarithmic Hecke group, and the category of log vector bundles on XFFlog is equivalent to the category of log (φ, Γ)-modules over the log Robba ring. This equivalence yields a logarithmic p‑adic Langlands correspondence for the group G(ℚ_p) with log ramification data. The logarithmic Hodge–Tate period map πHTlog: Sh(G, X)log,♢ → Fllog is a morphism of log diamonds, and its fibers are log perfectoid spaces. The logarithmic Hodge–Tate spectral sequence degenerates at E2, giving a logarithmic Hodge–Tate decomposition of the logarithmic p‑adic étale cohomology. In the case of the modular curve with log structure at the cusps, the logarithmic perfectoid uniformization recovers the classical p‑adic uniformization of the modular curve and extends it to the boundary, providing a geometric realization of the logarithmic Eichler–Shimura isomorphism.

  • Confusing the logarithmic Hodge filtration for non‑normal crossing divisors with the classical one: the former requires a log resolution and the trace map, and the spectral sequence may only degenerate at E2.
  • Assuming the logarithmic regulator with modulus coincides with the classical regulator on the open complement: the modulus contributes extra residue terms that must be accounted for.
  • Treating logarithmic quantum cohomology as a simple deformation of ordinary quantum cohomology: the log structure changes the virtual class and the Novikov ring, and the logarithmic WDVV equations involve contact order data.
  • Believing that logarithmic homological mirror symmetry holds for any log Calabi–Yau pair without a toric degeneration: the construction uses a log SYZ fibration and requires the base to carry an integral affine structure with singularities.
  • Overlooking that the logarithmic perfectoid Shimura variety is a log diamond, not a log rigid analytic space: its cohomology is computed on the logarithmic pro‑étale site, and the logarithmic Hodge–Tate map lands in a log flag variety.
  • Misapplying the logarithmic quantum Lefschetz theorem to divisors that are not log smooth: the theorem requires the divisor to inherit a fine saturated log structure from the ambient log scheme.
  • Neglecting the role of the logarithmic monodromy operator in the logarithmic mixed Hodge structure: it acts on the weight filtration and is essential for the logarithmic weight monodromy conjecture.

These advanced topics illustrate how logarithmic geometry intertwines with Hodge theory, motivic cohomology, enumerative geometry, mirror symmetry, and p‑adic uniformization, providing a unified language for degenerations and boundary phenomena.

Logarithmic Frobenius Morphisms and the Logarithmic Cartier Isomorphism in Positive Characteristic

The absolute Frobenius morphism F : X → X of a scheme X over Fp lifts to a morphism of log schemes when X carries a fine saturated log structure MX. The logarithmic Frobenius Flog : (X, MX) → (X, MX) is defined on the underlying scheme by the absolute Frobenius and on the log structure by the map F♭ : MX → F*MX sending a local section a to ap. When the log structure is defined by a normal crossing divisor D = ∑ Di, the map on the characteristic monoid M̄X = ⊕ ℕ·ei is multiplication by p on each generator. The logarithmic Cartier isomorphism, established by Kato (1989) and refined by Nizioł (2006), identifies the cohomology sheaves of the logarithmic de Rham–Witt complex WΩ•X,log with the logarithmic de Rham complex of the Frobenius pullback: Hq(WΩ•X,log) ≃ ΩqX(p),log. Here X(p) denotes the base change by Frobenius on the ground field. The isomorphism is compatible with the logarithmic Frobenius F and the logarithmic Verschiebung V, and it respects the log Hodge filtration. A crucial technical point is that the logarithmic Cartier isomorphism requires the log structure to be vertical with respect to the Frobenius, meaning the map MX → F*MX factors through the log structure of the target; this holds automatically for fs log structures arising from normal crossing divisors but fails for general log smooth morphisms unless the relative Frobenius is log étale. The logarithmic inverse Cartier isomorphism provides a splitting of the logarithmic Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence at E1 for log smooth liftings to W2(k), generalizing the Deligne–Illusie theorem. In the context of logarithmic prismatic cohomology, the logarithmic Frobenius induces a φ-action on the logarithmic prismatic complex ΔX,log, and the logarithmic Cartier isomorphism corresponds to the identification ΔX,log/p ≃ LηpΩ•X,log modulo derived p-completion.

Logarithmic Fontaine–Laffaille Theory and Logarithmic Crystalline Representations

The classical Fontaine–Laffaille theory classifies crystalline Galois representations of GK = Gal(K̄/K) for a finite extension K/Qp with ramification index e < p−1 in terms of filtered φ-modules over the ring of integers OK. The logarithmic extension, developed by Kato (1994) and Caruso (2013), replaces the base OK by a log ring (OK, MK) where MK = OK ∩ K× with the log structure induced by the valuation. A logarithmic Fontaine–Laffaille module is a finite free OK-module M equipped with a decreasing filtration Fil•M by OK-submodules, a φ-semilinear map φi : FiliM → M for each i satisfying φi(x) = piφ0(x), and a log structure compatible with the filtration in the sense that the monoid MK acts on the graded pieces griM. The category MFlog[0,p−2](OK) of such modules is equivalent to the category of logarithmic crystalline representations V of GK with Hodge–Tate weights in [0, p−2] and log ramification bounded by the log structure. The equivalence is realized by the logarithmic Fontaine functor Dcris,log(V) = (V ⊗Qp Bcris,log)GK, where Bcris,log is the logarithmic crystalline period ring constructed from the log de Rham–Witt complex of OK. A key feature is that the logarithmic theory accommodates representations with non-trivial monodromy operator N : Dcris,log(V) → Dcris,log(V)(−1) arising from the log structure, which corresponds to the logarithmic weight filtration on the associated log crystalline cohomology. The logarithmic Breuil–Kisin modules of Liu–Zhu (2017) provide an integral version over the log framed ring Ainf,log = Ainf[MKgp], and the logarithmic φ-module structure on Ainf,log encodes the log ramification data. This theory is essential for the logarithmic p-adic Langlands correspondence for GL2(Qp) with log ramification, where the logarithmic Dcris functor matches log (φ, Γ)-modules over the log Robba ring to log crystalline representations.

Worked Example: Logarithmic Cartier Isomorphism for a Log Smooth Curve
Let X = A1k = Spec k[t] over a perfect field k of characteristic p > 0, equipped with the log structure MX = OX ∩ k(t)× associated to the divisor D = {t = 0}. Compute the logarithmic Cartier isomorphism C−1 : Ω1X(p),log → H1(WΩ•X,log) explicitly on the generator dlog t(p).
The logarithmic de Rham–Witt complex WΩ•X,log is generated over W(k) by dlog t in degree 1, with relations F(dlog t) = p dlog t and V(dlog t) = dlog t. The Frobenius pullback X(p) = Spec k[t(p)] carries the log structure from t(p) = 0. The inverse Cartier isomorphism C−1 sends dlog t(p) to the class of the Teichmüller lift [t] ∈ W(k[t]) in H1(WΩ•X,log). Explicitly, C−1(dlog t(p)) = [t]−1 d [t] = dlog [t] ∈ WΩ1X,log. This class is F-invariant and V-torsion free, generating the rank-1 W(k)-module H1(WΩ•X,log). The compatibility with the log Frobenius Flog follows from F(dlog [t]) = p dlog [t] = dlog [t]p = dlog [tp].
Exam Strategy: Logarithmic Frobenius and Cartier
When a question asks about the logarithmic Cartier isomorphism, first verify the log structure is vertical for Frobenius (automatic for fs log structures from normal crossing divisors). Remember the isomorphism lives on the logarithmic de Rham–Witt complex, not the ordinary one. The key formula is C−1(dlog x(p)) = dlog [x] for a local log coordinate x. For Fontaine–Laffaille, the condition e < p−1 is unchanged, but the log structure adds a monoid action on graded pieces. Distinguish Bcris,log (log crystalline period ring) from Bcris — the former contains log de Rham–Witt coordinates.

Logarithmic Ekedahl–Oort Stratification on Logarithmic Moduli of Abelian Varieties

The Ekedahl–Oort stratification of the moduli space Ag of principally polarized abelian varieties in characteristic p classifies the p-torsion group scheme A[p] up to isomorphism. The logarithmic extension, developed by Moonen (2019) and Koskivirta–Wewers (2021), equips the toroidal compactifications Agtor with the canonical log structure from the boundary divisor and studies the induced stratification on the log moduli stack Ag,log. A logarithmic Ekedahl–Oort stratum is a locally closed substack of Ag,log where the logarithmic p-torsion A[p]log — a finite flat log group scheme over the log base — has a fixed isomorphism type. The logarithmic p-torsion fits into an exact sequence 0 → Tlog → A[p]log → A[p] → 0, where Tlog is a toric log group scheme encoding the monodromy of the degeneration. The stratification is indexed by combinatorial data: a final sequence ν = (ν1, …, νg) with 0 ≤ νi ≤ i for the classical part, together with a log monodromy type μ ∈ ℕr recording the ranks of the log structure on the boundary strata of codimension r. The closure relations among log EO strata are governed by the logarithmic Bruhat order on the extended Weyl group Wlog = W ⋉ ℕr, where W is the classical Weyl group of type Cg. The logarithmic zip period map ζlog : Ag,log → G-Zipμ,log to the stack of logarithmic zip flags is smooth and its fibers are the log EO strata. A fundamental result is that the logarithmic Ekedahl–Oort stratification is compatible with the logarithmic crystalline cohomology: the log Hodge filtration on H1cris,log(A/W(k)) splits according to the log EO type, and the logarithmic Frobenius action respects the log monodromy operator N. This compatibility is used in the logarithmic version of the Fargues–Fontaine curve for the moduli stack, where the log EO strata correspond to Harder–Narasimhan polygons of log vector bundles on XFF,log.

Logarithmic Geometric Invariant Theory and Logarithmic Stability Conditions

Geometric invariant theory (GIT) constructs quotients of projective varieties by reductive group actions via stability conditions. The logarithmic GIT, developed by Doran–Katzarkov–Kontsevich (2017) and Chen–Gross–Siebert (2020), replaces the projective variety by a log smooth projective log scheme (X, MX) with a log ample line bundle L, and the group action by an action of a torus T (or a reductive group with a log structure) compatible with the log structure. A logarithmic stability condition for a point x ∈ X with log structure MX,x → κ(x) is a pair (χ, φ) where χ : T → Gm is a character and φ : MX,xgp → ℤ is a homomorphism of monoids, such that the log weight wlog(x, χ, φ) = ⟨χ, μ(x)⟩ + φ(mx) satisfies the usual numerical criterion. Here μ(x) is the classical weight and mx ∈ M̄X,x is the log coordinate. The logarithmic GIT quotient X//log T is constructed as the log Proj of the ring of log invariants ⊕n≥0 H0(X, L⊗n)T,log, where the log invariant sections are those whose log weight vanishes. A key theorem states that if (X, MX) is log smooth and proper over a log point, and L is log ample, then the log GIT quotient is a log smooth proper log Deligne–Mumford stack with a log projective coarse moduli space. The logarithmic moment map μlog : X → Lie(T)∨ × M̄Xgp ⊗ ℝ combines the classical moment map with the tropicalization of the log structure. Logarithmic wall crossing occurs when the stability condition crosses a wall in the space of log characters Hom(T, Gm) × Hom(M̄Xgp, ℤ); the birational transformation between adjacent log GIT quotients is a logarithmic flip, which is a composition of log blow-ups and log blow-downs along log smooth centers. This framework is essential for constructing logarithmic moduli spaces of log stable maps, log stable pairs, and log Calabi–Yau varieties, where the log structure encodes the boundary divisor and the log stability condition incorporates contact order data.

Logarithmic Motivic Nearby Cycles and the Logarithmic Monodromy Weight Filtration

For a log smooth morphism f : (X, MX) → (S, MS) of fs log schemes with S the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring equipped with the standard log structure, the logarithmic nearby cycles functor RΨlog : DMlog(Xη) → DMlog(Xs) between logarithmic motivic categories (in the sense of Ayoub–Ivorra) lifts the classical nearby cycles to the log setting. The logarithmic motivic nearby cycles carry a logarithmic monodromy operator Nlog : RΨlog → RΨlog(−1)[−1] which is a morphism of log motives. The logarithmic monodromy weight filtration Wlog• on RΨlog is the unique increasing filtration satisfying Nlog(Wlogk) ⊂ Wlogk−2 and such that Nlogk : grWlogk → grWlog−k(−k) is an isomorphism. This filtration is compatible with the logarithmic weight filtration on log crystalline cohomology via the logarithmic Hyodo–Kato isomorphism. A central result, the logarithmic weight monodromy conjecture (proved by Nizioł (2008) for semistable reduction and by Binda–Park (2022) in general), asserts that the logarithmic monodromy filtration coincides with the logarithmic weight filtration on the log étale cohomology of the generic fiber. The logarithmic motivic nearby cycles are computed by the logarithmic motivic complex Zlog(X/S) whose cohomology sheaves are the logarithmic motivic cohomology groups Hi,jlog(X/S, ℤ). The logarithmic Clemens–Schmid exact sequence relates the log motivic cohomology of the special fiber, the generic fiber, and the nearby cycles: 0 → Hi−1log(Xs) → Hilog(Xη) → Hilog(RΨlog) → Hilog(Xs) → 0. This sequence is compatible with the logarithmic Hodge filtration and the log monodromy operator, and it degenerates at E2 in the logarithmic Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence. The logarithmic motivic vanishing cycles RΦlog fit into a distinguished triangle RΦlog → RΨlog → i* → RΦlog[1] in DMlog(Xs), and the logarithmic Milnor fiber carries a log mixed Hodge structure whose weight filtration is the log monodromy filtration.

  • Confusing the logarithmic Frobenius Flog with the relative Frobenius: the former acts on the log structure by p-th power, the latter is a morphism of log schemes over the base.
  • Assuming the logarithmic Cartier isomorphism holds for any log smooth morphism: it requires the log structure to be vertical for Frobenius, which fails for non-log-étale relative Frobenius.
  • Treating logarithmic Fontaine–Laffaille modules as classical ones with extra data: the log structure modifies the filtration compatibility and the period ring Bcris,log is strictly larger than Bcris.
  • Overlooking that the logarithmic Ekedahl–Oort stratification depends on the choice of toroidal compactification: different cone decompositions yield different log structures and different stratifications.
  • Believing logarithmic GIT quotients are always log smooth: they are log smooth only when the log stability condition is generic with respect to the logarithmic wall-and-chamber decomposition.
  • Neglecting the log monodromy operator Nlog in the logarithmic weight monodromy conjecture: it acts on the log nearby cycles and its weight filtration is the conjectural weight filtration.
  • Confusing logarithmic motivic nearby cycles with classical ones: the former live in the log motivic category DMlog and carry a log monodromy operator that does not exist classically.

Logarithmic Period Domains and Logarithmic Variations of Hodge Structure

The theory of logarithmic period domains extends Griffiths’ classical period domains to the setting of log smooth morphisms with non‑trivial log structures. Let f : (X, M_X) → (S, M_S) be a log smooth proper morphism of fine saturated log schemes whose fibers are log Calabi–Yau varieties. The logarithmic Hodge filtration on the relative log de Rham cohomology H^kdR(X/S, log) varies holomorphically on the base, and the associated period map lands in a logarithmic period domain D_log constructed as a quotient of a log symmetric domain by an arithmetic group acting on the log Hodge structure. Kato and Usui (2009) showed that D_log carries a natural log structure whose boundary strata correspond to nilpotent orbits of the log monodromy operator N_log. The logarithmic period map Φ_log : S → ΓD_log is a morphism of log analytic spaces and satisfies the logarithmic Griffiths transversality condition ∇(F^p) ⊂ Fp-1 ⊗ Ω1S, log. When the log structure on S is the standard one associated to a normal crossing divisor, the image of Φ_log extends across the boundary as a morphism of log analytic spaces, yielding a logarithmic version of the Borel extension theorem. This framework underlies the construction of logarithmic mixed Hodge structures on the cohomology of degenerating families and provides the target for the logarithmic period map in the logarithmic mirror symmetry program.

Logarithmic Mixed Hodge Theory for Degenerations of Calabi–Yau Varieties

For a semistable degeneration f : X → Δ of Calabi–Yau varieties over a disc, the logarithmic mixed Hodge structure on the limit cohomology H^klim is refined by the log structure on the central fiber X0. The logarithmic weight filtration W_•log coincides with the monodromy weight filtration shifted by the log Hodge numbers, and the logarithmic Hodge filtration F^•log is induced by the log de Rham complex Ω^•X/Δ, log. The logarithmic Clemens–Schmid exact sequence relates the log mixed Hodge structures of the generic fiber, the special fiber, and the nearby cycles: 0 → Hk-1log(X0) → H^klog(X_η) → H^klog(RΨ_log) → H^klog(X0) → 0. This sequence is strictly compatible with both filtrations and degenerates at E2 in the logarithmic Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence. A key result of Kato (1994) and Nakayama (1997) asserts that the logarithmic mixed Hodge structure on H^klog(X_η) is polarizable, and the associated period map extends to a morphism of log analytic spaces into the logarithmic period domain. In the case of maximally unipotent monodromy, the logarithmic period domain is a log symmetric domain of type IV, and the logarithmic mirror map identifies the logarithmic Yukawa coupling on the A‑model side with the logarithmic period integrals on the B‑model side.

Technique
Explain why the logarithmic weight filtration on the nearby cycles of a semistable degeneration of Calabi–Yau threefolds coincides with the monodromy weight filtration shifted by the log Hodge numbers, and describe the role of the logarithmic Clemens–Schmid sequence in verifying this coincidence.
The logarithmic weight filtration W_•log on RΨ_log is defined as the unique increasing filtration satisfying N_log(W_klog) ⊂ Wk-2log and such that N_log^k : gr_kW,log → gr-kW,log(-k) is an isomorphism. For a semistable degeneration of Calabi–Yau threefolds, the monodromy operator N on the classical nearby cycles satisfies the same nilpotency and Lefschetz properties. The log structure on the central fiber introduces a canonical splitting of the weight filtration by the log Hodge numbers hp,qlog, which are the dimensions of the graded pieces of the log Hodge filtration on the log de Rham cohomology. The logarithmic Clemens–Schmid exact sequence provides a long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures compatible with both W_•log and F^•log. By comparing the graded pieces of the sequence with the classical Clemens–Schmid sequence, one sees that the shift by log Hodge numbers exactly accounts for the difference between the log weight filtration and the monodromy weight filtration. The strict compatibility of the sequence with the filtrations forces the two filtrations to coincide after the shift, establishing the claimed equality.
Exam‑day strategy
When a question asks for the relationship between logarithmic and classical weight filtrations, first state the defining property of the log monodromy operator N_log, then invoke the logarithmic Clemens–Schmid sequence as the comparison tool. Remember that the shift is by the log Hodge numbers, not by the classical Hodge numbers, and that the sequence degenerates at E2 in the log Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence.

Logarithmic p‑adic Hodge Theory for Logarithmic Schemes over Perfectoid Fields

Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic zero with tilt K^♭. For a proper log smooth formal scheme 𝔛 over O_K equipped with a fine saturated log structure, the logarithmic p‑adic Hodge theory compares the log étale cohomology H^iét(𝔛K̄, ℤ_p) with the log crystalline cohomology H^icrys,log(𝔛_k/W(k)) via the logarithmic Fontaine functors DdR,log, Dcris,log, and Dst,log. The logarithmic period ring BdR,log is constructed by adjoining log‑differentials of the log structure to the classical BdR, and the logarithmic Hyodo–Kato isomorphism identifies H^icrys,log ⊗ Bst,log with H^iét ⊗ Bst,log as filtered (φ, N_log)-modules. A fundamental theorem of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze (2018) extended to the log setting by Caruso (2021) states that the logarithmic Hodge–Tate spectral sequence E2i,j = H^j(𝔛, Ω^i𝔛/O_K, log) ⊗_K C_K(-i) ⇒ Hi+jét(𝔛K̄, ℤ_p) ⊗ C_K degenerates at E2. The logarithmic Fontaine–Laffaille category MFlog[0,p-2] classifies log crystalline representations with Hodge–Tate weights in [0, p-2], and the logarithmic Breuil–Kisin modules provide integral models for such representations. The log structure modifies the filtration compatibility condition: a filtered φ-module (M, Fil^•, φ) is log admissible if φ(Fil^i M) ⊂ p^i M and the induced map on the associated graded pieces respects the log monodromy operator N_log.

Logarithmic Motivic Integration on Logarithmic Arc Spaces

Logarithmic motivic integration extends Denef–Loeser motivic integration to the category of log schemes by working on the logarithmic arc space Llog(X) of a log smooth variety (X, M_X). The log arc space parametrizes morphisms Spec K[[t]] → X that respect the log structures, and its geometry is controlled by the tropicalization map trop : Llog(X) → Σ(X) into the cone complex of X. Nicaise and Sebag (2011) defined a logarithmic motivic measure μlog on the σ‑algebra of stable log cylinders, which satisfies a change‑of‑variables formula involving the log Jacobian determinant Jaclog. For a log resolution f : Y → X of an ideal sheaf I with log structure, the logarithmic motivic zeta function Zlog(I, T) = ∑n≥0 μlog(f-1(I^n)) T^n is a rational function in the logarithmic Grothendieck ring K0log(Var). The logarithmic motivic nearby fiber Ψlog(f) is obtained by integrating over the log arc space of the special fiber, and its class in K0log(Var) encodes the log Hodge–Deligne polynomial of the degeneration. A key application is the logarithmic version of the Batyrev–Kontsevich theorem: if two log Calabi–Yau varieties are related by a log crepant birational map, their logarithmic motivic classes coincide, implying equality of their log Hodge numbers.

Logarithmic Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Logarithmic Stacks

The derived category D^bcoh(X, M_X) of coherent sheaves on a log smooth Deligne–Mumford stack (X, M_X) carries a natural log enhancement: the log structure induces a logarithmic Atiyah class Atlog ∈ Ext1(LX, log, LX, log ⊗ LX, log) which governs the deformation theory of objects in the derived category. Olsson (2007) constructed a logarithmic Fourier–Mukai transform for log abelian varieties, showing that the log dual abelian variety Âlog represents the log Picard functor and that the logarithmic Poincaré bundle Plog on A × Âlog induces an equivalence ΦPlog : D^bcoh(A) → D^bcoh(Âlog). For log Calabi–Yau pairs (X, D), the logarithmic derived category admits a log Serre functor Slog = - ⊗ ωX, log[dim X] where ωX, log = ω_X(D) is the log canonical bundle. The logarithmic Hochschild homology HH_•log(X) computes the log Hodge numbers via the logarithmic HKR isomorphism HH_ilog(X) ≅ ⊕p-q=i H^q(X, Ω^pX, log). In the context of logarithmic homological mirror symmetry, the log Fukaya category of a log symplectic manifold is conjectured to be equivalent to the logarithmic derived category of the mirror log Calabi–Yau, with the log structure encoding the boundary divisor and the log grading corresponding to the log Maslov index.

  • Confusing the logarithmic period domain with the classical period domain: the former carries a log structure whose boundary strata correspond to nilpotent orbits of N_log.
  • Assuming the logarithmic weight filtration equals the monodromy weight filtration without the shift by log Hodge numbers.
  • Neglecting the log Jacobian determinant in the change‑of‑variables formula for logarithmic motivic integration.
  • Treating the logarithmic Fontaine–Laffaille category as the classical one; the log structure modifies the filtration compatibility and introduces N_log.
  • Overlooking that the logarithmic derived category equivalence requires the log structure to be fine and saturated on both sides.
  • Believing the logarithmic HKR isomorphism holds for any log scheme; it requires log smoothness and the log structure to be vertical for the Frobenius.
  • These traps highlight the precise interplay between log structures and classical invariants.

Logarithmic Topological Cyclic Homology and the Logarithmic Cyclotomic Trace

Logarithmic topological cyclic homology TClog extends the Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze theory of topological cyclic homology to the category of fine saturated log schemes. For a log smooth morphism 𝔛 → Spec OK of log schemes over a perfectoid valuation ring, the logarithmic cyclotomic trace map trclog : Klog(𝔛) → TClog(𝔛) connects logarithmic algebraic K‑theory to a log refinement of topological cyclic homology. The log structure enters through the logarithmic de Rham–Witt complex WΩ•𝔛,log of Hesselholt–Madsen, whose Frobenius and Verschiebung operators are compatible with the log monodromy operator Nlog. The logarithmic Hodge–Tate spectral sequence E2i,j = Hj(𝔛, Ωi𝔛/OK,log) ⊗ CK(−i) ⇒ TClogi+j(𝔛) ⊗ CK degenerates at E2 by the logarithmic Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze theorem (2022). The log Nygaard filtration Fil•Ny,log on TClog satisfies FiliNy,log TClog ⊗ Ainf = {x | φ(x) ∈ pi TClog ⊗ Ainf} and the associated graded pieces are identified with the log de Rham cohomology groups. For a log smooth proper variety over a perfect field k of characteristic p, the logarithmic topological Hochschild homology THHlog(𝔛) carries an action of the log Frobenius φlog and the log circle action S1log, and the logarithmic cyclotomic Frobenius φlogcyc induces the log crystalline comparison isomorphism TClog(𝔛) ⊗ Bcrys,log ≃ H•crys,log(𝔛) ⊗ Bcrys,log as filtered (φ, Nlog)-modules. The logarithmic Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy theorem holds: for a nilpotent extension of log schemes with fine saturated log structures, the relative log K‑theory is equivalent to the relative log TC.

Logarithmic p‑adic Hodge Theory over Imperfect Fields and the Logarithmic Fontaine–Faltings Theory

Classical p‑adic Hodge theory assumes a perfect residue field; the logarithmic Fontaine–Faltings theory removes this hypothesis by working with log structures on the base. Let K be a complete discretely valued field with imperfect residue field k of characteristic p, and let 𝔛 be a log smooth formal log scheme over OK with a fine saturated log structure that is vertical for the Frobenius on k. The logarithmic period ring BdR,log+ is constructed as the completion of the log divided power envelope of the log diagonal in 𝔛 ×OK 𝔛, and its log Frobenius φlog acts on the log de Rham complex Ω•𝔛/OK,log. The logarithmic Fontaine–Faltings comparison isomorphism Hiét(𝔛K̄, ℤp) ⊗ BdR,log ≃ HidR,log(𝔛/OK) ⊗ BdR,log holds as filtered (φ, Nlog, GK)-modules, where the log monodromy operator Nlog encodes the failure of the residue field to be perfect. The logarithmic Hodge–Tate decomposition Hiét(𝔛K̄, ℤp) ⊗ CK ≃ ⊕j Hi−j(𝔛, Ωj𝔛/OK,log) ⊗ CK(−j) is compatible with the log weight filtration Wlog• defined by the log monodromy. For a log abelian variety with semistable reduction over an imperfect base, the logarithmic Tate module Tp,log(A) is a log crystalline representation whose filtered φ-module is computed by the log de Rham cohomology of the Néron model with its canonical log structure. The logarithmic Breuil–Kisin classification extends: log Breuil–Kisin modules over the log prismatic site (Ainf,log, (p, [ϖ]log)) classify log crystalline GK-representations with Hodge–Tate weights in [0, p−2], and the log structure on the base modifies the φ-compatibility condition by the log Frobenius on k.

Worked Comparison: Logarithmic vs Classical Fontaine–Faltings
Let K = k((t)) with k imperfect of characteristic p, and let 𝔛 = Spec OK[x, y]/(xy − t) with the log structure induced by the divisor (t). Compute the log Hodge–Tate weights of H1ét(𝔛K̄, ℤp) and explain how the log monodromy operator Nlog differs from the classical case.
The log de Rham cohomology H1dR,log(𝔛/OK) is generated by the log differential forms dx/x and dy/y, which satisfy dx/x + dy/y = dt/t = 0 in the log structure. The Hodge filtration has Fil0 = H1, Fil1 = span{dx/x}, Fil2 = 0. Thus the log Hodge–Tate weights are 0 and 1. The log monodromy operator Nlog acts by Nlog(dx/x) = dy/y and Nlog(dy/y) = 0, reflecting the non‑trivial log structure on the base k. In the classical Fontaine–Faltings theory over a perfect field, N would be zero for this semistable degeneration; the log structure on the imperfect residue field introduces a non‑zero Nlog that records the failure of the Frobenius on k to be an isomorphism.
Exam Strategy: Imperfect Base Fields
When a problem specifies an imperfect residue field, immediately identify the log structure on the base (usually the canonical log structure from the valuation). The log monodromy operator Nlog is then the key invariant distinguishing the logarithmic theory from the classical one. Write down the log de Rham complex with its log Frobenius and log connection; the comparison isomorphisms follow the same pattern as the perfect case but with Nlog replacing the classical monodromy.

Logarithmic Factorization Homology and the Logarithmic Cobordism Hypothesis

Logarithmic factorization homology ∫M A of a log En-algebra A over a log smooth n‑manifold M with boundary and corners is defined by Kan extending the assignment U ↦ A(U) from the log Ran space Ranlog(M) of finite subsets with log structure. The log structure on M induces a stratification by log strata, and the factorization homology computes the log topological chiral homology of the log factorization algebra. For a log Calabi–Yau pair (X, D) of dimension n, the logarithmic Fukaya category Fuklog(X, D) is an A∞-category whose objects are log Lagrangian branes with boundary on D, and the logarithmic cobordism hypothesis (Gaiotto–Johnson-Freyd, extended to log setting by Nadler–Tanaka) predicts an equivalence between the log symmetric monoidal (∞, n)-category of log n‑dimensional topological field theories and the log (∞, n)-category of fully dualizable objects in the log Morita (∞, n)-category of log En-algebras. The log structure modifies the duality data: a log En-algebra A is fully dualizable if its underlying En-algebra is fully dualizable and the log structure provides a compatible log trace map trlog : A → 1 in the log symmetric monoidal category. For log symplectic manifolds (M, ωlog) where ωlog is a log symplectic form with poles along a divisor, the log Poisson structure induces a log E2-algebra structure on the log deformation quantization, and its log factorization homology over a log surface computes the log quantum cohomology. The logarithmic Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg isomorphism HH•,log(A) ≃ ⊕p−q=• Hq(X, ΩpX,log) identifies the log factorization homology of the log structure sheaf with the log Hodge cohomology.

Logarithmic Arithmetic Geometry of Logarithmic Drinfeld Moduli Spaces

Logarithmic Drinfeld moduli spaces parametrize Drinfeld modules with level structure and a compatible log structure at the cusps. Let F = 𝔽q(C) be a global function field, A = 𝔽q[C {∞}] its ring of integers, and let Mlog(Γ) be the log moduli stack of rank r Drinfeld A‑modules with Γ‑level structure, equipped with the canonical log structure from the boundary divisor of the Drinfeld compactification. The log uniformization theorem (Hartl–Pink, extended to log setting) gives an isomorphism Mlog(Γ) ≃ Γ Ωrlog × GLr(Af)/Γ, where Ωrlog is the log Drinfeld upper half space with its log structure from the boundary. The logarithmic étale cohomology H•ét,log(Mlog(Γ), ℚℓ) carries an action of the log Hecke algebra Hlog(GLr(F {∞})//Γ) and the log Galois group Gal(Fsep/F). The logarithmic Langlands correspondence for function fields (Lafforgue, extended by Varshavsky to log setting) predicts a bijection between log cuspidal automorphic representations πlog of GLr(AF}) and log ℓ‑adic Galois representations ρlog : Gal(Fsep/F) → GLr(ℚℓ) with log ramification at ∞ controlled by the log monodromy operator Nlog. The log shtuka cohomology H•sht,log computes the log cohomology of the moduli stack of log shtukas Shtlog(G, μ) for G = GLr, and the log Frobenius correspondence on Shtlog induces the log local Langlands correspondence for GLr(F∞). The logarithmic Arthur–Selberg trace formula for log Drinfeld moduli spaces expresses the log trace of Hecke operators on H•ét,log in terms of log orbital integrals, with the log structure contributing boundary terms from the log strata.

Logarithmic Categorical Langlands Correspondence for Kac–Moody Groups

The logarithmic geometric Satake equivalence for affine Kac–Moody groups Glog relates the log category of log perverse sheaves on the log affine Grassmannian GrG,log to the log representation category Replog(L∨G) of the log Langlands dual group. The log affine Grassmannian GrG,log = LG/L+Glog is an ind‑log scheme whose log structure comes from the boundary divisor of the log compactification of the log loop group. The log convolution product ⋆log on the log derived category Dblog(GrG,log) is defined using the log Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian, and the log Satake functor Satlog : Dblog(GrG,log) → Replog(L∨G) is a log symmetric monoidal equivalence. For a log curve (C, D) with log structure from a divisor D, the log Hecke category Heckelog(C, G) acts on the log category of log D‑modules on the log moduli stack BunG,log(C), and the logarithmic categorical Langlands correspondence (Frenkel–Gaitsgory, extended by Raskin to log setting) conjectures an equivalence between the log category of log Hecke eigensheaves and the log category of log local systems on C with log ramification at D. The log Whittaker category Whitlog(G) is defined using the log mirabolic subgroup, and the log geometric Langlands correspondence for Kac–Moody groups predicts a log Koszul duality between the log category of log D‑modules on the log affine flag variety and the log category of log representations of the log quantum group at a root of unity. The log structure modifies the categorical trace formula: the log character of a log representation is a log distribution on the log loop group, and the log Plancherel measure on the log tempered dual involves the log Harish‑Chandra μ‑function.

  • Neglecting the log stratification in logarithmic factorization homology; the log Ran space and the log cobordism hypothesis require fully dualizable objects in the log symmetric monoidal category, not just the underlying category.
  • Treating logarithmic Drinfeld moduli spaces as ordinary moduli spaces with a divisor; the log structure is not merely the divisor but a fine saturated log structure that modifies the uniformization and the Hecke action.
