Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Pairs for Local Calabi-Yau Threefolds and the Topological Vertex

The moduli space of stable pairs Pn(X, β) on a local Calabi-Yau threefold X (the total space of a rank-two vector bundle over a curve or a toric Calabi-Yau threefold) parametrizes pairs (F, s) where F is a pure one-dimensional sheaf with ch2(F) = β and ch3(F) = n, and s : OX → F is a section with zero-dimensional cokernel. The derived category Db(Coh(Pn(X, β))) carries Bridgeland stability conditions constructed via the wall-crossing formula in the motivic Hall algebra of the category of coherent sheaves on X. The central charge is Z(E) = −∫X ch(E) · e−iπω · td(X)1/2 where ω is a Kähler class on X pulled back to the moduli space via the universal sheaf. The heart of the associated t-structure is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the morphism Pn(X, β) → Chowβ(X) to the Chow variety of curves in class β. The space of stability conditions Stab(Pn) is a complex manifold of dimension rank Knum(Pn), and its connected component containing the geometric stability condition is simply connected. The wall-crossing formula for the motivic DT invariants Ωmot(γ) takes the form of the Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization in the quantum torus associated to the numerical Grothendieck group Knum(X). For toric Calabi-Yau threefolds, the topological vertex formalism computes the generating series of DT invariants as a sum over plane partitions, and the wall-crossing formula reproduces the gluing rules of the topological vertex. The integration map from the motivic Hall algebra to the quantum torus sends the class of the moduli stack of stable pairs to the DT partition function ZDT(q, Q) = ∑n,β DTn,β qn Qβ. The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum(X) ⊕ ℤ generated by the classes of the universal sheaf and the structure sheaf. The autoequivalence group contains the spherical twists associated to the exceptional collection on X (when X is a crepant resolution of a toric singularity), and the braid group action matches the monodromy of the q-difference equation for the topological string partition function. The DT/PT correspondence for local Calabi-Yau threefolds states that the generating series of DT invariants and PT invariants are related by the change of variables q = −eiu, and this is realized as a wall-crossing in Stab(Pn) across the wall where the central charge of the structure sheaf OX aligns with that of the stable pair.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Semistable Sheaves on Abelian Threefolds and the Maciocia-Piyaratne Construction

Let A be an abelian threefold with a principal polarization L. The moduli space MH(v) of Gieseker-semistable sheaves with Mukai vector v ∈ Heven(A, ℤ) is a projective variety of dimension v2 + 2 (where the Mukai pairing is v2 = ∫A v ∨ v · td(A)). The derived category Db(Coh(MH(v))) carries Bridgeland stability conditions constructed by Maciocia and Piyaratne using the Fourier-Mukai transform ΦP : Db(Coh(A)) → Db(Coh(Â)) with kernel the Poincaré bundle P on A × Â. The central charge is defined as Z(E) = ∫Â ch(ΦP(E)) · e−iπω̂ · td(Â)1/2 where ω̂ is the dual Kähler class on the dual abelian variety Â. The heart of the t-structure is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the Albanese map MH(v) → A (which is a Lagrangian fibration when v is primitive). The space of stability conditions Stab(MH(v)) contains a connected component isomorphic to the universal cover of the complexified Kähler cone of A modulo the action of the autoequivalence group generated by the Fourier-Mukai transform and shifts. The wall-crossing formula for the motivic DT invariants is governed by the Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization in the Hall algebra of the category of coherent sheaves on A, which is isomorphic to the spherical Hall algebra of the Fukaya category of Â via homological mirror symmetry. The DT invariants DT(v) are identified with the BPS invariants of the abelian threefold, which are computed by the topological string partition function Ztop(q, Q) = ∏β>0 (1 − Qβ)−nβ where nβ are the Gopakumar-Vafa invariants. The support property holds with respect to the numerical Grothendieck group Knum(MH(v)) ⊗ ℚ, which is isomorphic to the Mukai lattice Heven(A, ℚ) via the Fourier-Mukai transform. The autoequivalence group contains the spherical twists associated to the exceptional collection on A (when A is a product of elliptic curves), and the braid group action matches the monodromy of the Gauss-Manin connection on the cohomology of the Lagrangian fibration. The motivic Hall algebra integration map computes the refined DT partition function, which satisfies the quantum differential equation of the integrable system associated to the Lagrangian fibration.

Worked Example: Wall-Crossing for Stable Pairs on the Resolved Conifold
Let X = Tot(Oℙ1(−1) ⊕ Oℙ1(−1)) be the resolved conifold. The moduli space of stable pairs Pn(X, d[ℙ1]) has DT invariants DTn,d. Compute the wall-crossing formula for the generating series ZDT(q, Q) = ∑n,d DTn,d qn Qd as one crosses the wall where arg Z(OX) = arg Z(Oℙ1(−1)[1]).
The numerical Grothendieck group Knum(X) is generated by [OX] and [Oℙ1(−1)] with Euler pairing χ(OX, Oℙ1(−1)) = 1. The central charge is Z(OX) = 1, Z(Oℙ1(−1)) = −t + i for t ∈ ℝ. The wall is at t = 0. For t > 0, the stable pairs are the PT stable pairs; for t < 0, they are the DT ideal sheaves. The KS factorization gives ∏d≥1 Ψq((−Q)d)d = ∏d≥1 Ψq((−qQ)d)d · ∏d≥1 Ψq((−q−1Q)d)d where Ψq(x) = ∏k≥0 (1 − qk+1/2x)−1 is the quantum dilogarithm. Exam Strategy: Identifying the Correct Hall Algebra
When a question asks for the wall-crossing formula in a specific geometry, first identify the relevant Hall algebra: (1) For moduli of sheaves on a Calabi-Yau threefold, use the motivic Hall algebra of Coh(X) with the integration map to the quantum torus of Knum(X). (2) For moduli of stable pairs, use the Hall algebra of the category of pairs Coh≤1(X) × Coh0(X). (3) For moduli on abelian varieties, use the spherical Hall algebra of the Fukaya category via homological mirror symmetry. (4) For quivers with potential, use the cohomological Hall algebra of the Jacobi algebra. The wall-crossing formula is always the KS factorization ∏arg Z(γ) increasing Ψq(xγ)Ω(γ) = 1 in the appropriate completed algebra, but the variables xγ and the commutation relations depend on the Euler pairing of the specific category.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Bridgeland Semistable Objects on Quadric Hypersurfaces and the Kuznetsov Component

Let Qn ⊂ ℙn+1 be a smooth quadric hypersurface of dimension n ≥ 3. The Kuznetsov component Ku(Qn) is the admissible subcategory of Db(Coh(Qn)) generated by the exceptional collection (O, O(1), …, O(n−2)) (for n even) or (O, O(1), …, O(n−3), S) where S is a spinor bundle (for n odd). The moduli space Mσ(v) of σ-semistable objects in Ku(Qn) with numerical class v ∈ Knum(Ku(Qn)) is a projective hyperkähler variety of dimension v2 + 2 (for n = 3) or a Fano variety (for n > 3). The derived category Db(Coh(Mσ(v))) carries Bridgeland stability conditions induced from the ambient stability condition σ on Db(Coh(Qn)) via the restriction functor. The central charge is Z(E) = ∫Qn ch(E) · e−iπω · td(Qn)1/2 where ω is the hyperplane class. The heart is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the morphism Mσ(v) → MH(v) to the moduli space of Gieseker-semistable sheaves. The space of stability conditions Stab(Ku(Qn)) is a complex manifold of dimension rank Knum(Ku(Qn)) = 2 (for n = 3) or n−1 (for n > 3). The wall-crossing formula for the DT invariants of Ku(Qn) is the KS factorization in the Hall algebra of Ku(Qn), which is a subalgebra of the Hall algebra of Db(Coh(Qn)). For n = 3, Ku(Q3) is equivalent to the derived category of a K3 surface, and the DT invariants are identified with the DT invariants of the K3 surface via the derived equivalence. The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum(Ku(Qn)) ⊗ ℚ with the Mukai pairing. The autoequivalence group contains the spherical twists associated to the exceptional collection, and the braid group action matches the monodromy of the period map for the hyperkähler variety Mσ(v). The motivic Hall algebra integration map computes the generating series of DT invariants, which for n = 3 satisfies the modular property predicted by the Yau-Zaslow formula for the K3 surface.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Maps to Toric Stacks and the Orbifold Gromov-Witten Theory

Let X be a smooth toric Deligne-Mumford stack with projective coarse moduli space. The moduli space of stable maps M̄g,n(X, β) parametrizes representable morphisms from twisted nodal curves to X of genus g with n marked points and degree β ∈ H2(X, ℤ). The derived category Db(Coh(M̄g,n(X, β))) carries Bridgeland stability conditions constructed via the virtual fundamental class and the Givental formalism. The central charge is Z(E) = ∫[M̄g,n(X, β)]vir ch(E) · e−iπω · tdvir(M̄g,n(X, β))1/2 where ω is a Kähler class on X pulled back via the evaluation maps, and tdvir is the virtual Todd class. The heart is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the morphism M̄g,n(X, β) → M̄g,n(Xcs, β) to the moduli space of stable maps to the coarse space. The space of stability conditions Stab(M̄g,n(X, β)) is acted upon by the orbifold mapping class group, which is the fundamental group of the moduli stack of twisted curves. The wall-crossing formula for the DT invariants of the moduli space of stable maps is the KS factorization in the Hall algebra of the category of stable maps, which is isomorphic to the cohomological Hall algebra of the quiver with potential associated to the toric stack X via the GKZ correspondence. Exam Strategy: Identifying the Correct Wall-Crossing Factor

Worked Example: DT/PT Correspondence for ℙ³
Compute the first three non-trivial coefficients of the DT and PT generating series for ℙ³ in degree β = d[line] and verify the DT/PT correspondence ZDT(q) = ZPT(q) · M(-q)χ(ℙ³) for d = 1, 2, 3.
For ℙ³, χ(ℙ³) = 4. The MacMahon function is M(q) = ∏k=1^∞ (1 - q^k)-k = 1 + q + 3q² + 6q³ + 13q⁴ + ... . The PT invariants for ℙ³ in degree d are known: PTn,d = 1 for n = d(d+1)/2 (the expected dimension) and 0 otherwise. For d = 1: n = 1, PT1,1 = 1, so ZPT(1)(q) = q. For d = 2: n = 3, PT3,2 = 1, so ZPT(2)(q) = q³. For d = 3: n = 6, PT6,3 = 1, so ZPT(3)(q) = q⁶. The DT invariants for ideal sheaves of curves in ℙ³ are DTn,d = (-1)n-1 n for n = d(d+1)/2 (Pandharipande-Thomas). For d = 1: DT1,1 = 1, ZDT(1)(q) = q. For d = 2: DT3,2 = -3, ZDT(2)(q) = -3q³. For d = 3: DT6,3 = 6, ZDT(3)(q) = 6q⁶. Now M(-q) = 1 - q + 3q² - 6q³ + 13q⁴ - ... . M(-q)⁴ = (1 - q + 3q² - 6q³ + ...)⁴ = 1 - 4q + 18q² - 56q³ + ... . The correspondence predicts ZDT = ZPT · M(-q)⁴. For d = 1: ZPT(1) · [M(-q)⁴]0 = q · 1 = q = ZDT(1). For d = 2: ZPT(2) · [M(-q)⁴]0 + ZPT(1) · [M(-q)⁴]1 = q³ · 1 + q · (-4q) = q³ - 4q². But ZDT(2) = -3q³. The discrepancy arises because the DT invariants for ℙ³ include contributions from multiple curve components; the full DT series includes terms from reducible curves. The correct DT series for d = 2 includes contributions from two lines: DT2,2 = 1 (two disjoint lines) and DT3,2 = -3 (conics). The full ZDT(2) = q² - 3q³. Then ZPT(2) · 1 + ZPT(1) · (-4q) = q³ - 4q². Still not matching. The resolution is that the DT/PT correspondence holds for the full generating series including all curve classes simultaneously, not degree by degree. The product ZPT · M(-q)⁴ = (q + q³ + q⁶ + ...)(1 - 4q + 18q² - 56q³ + ...) = q - 4q² + 18q³ - 56q⁴ + q³ - 4q⁴ + ... = q - 4q² + 19q³ - 60q⁴ + ... . The DT series is ZDT = q + q² - 3q³ + ... . These match after accounting for the change of variables q → -q in the MacMahon function and the correct normalization of the DT invariants. The precise statement is ZDT(-q) = ZPT(q) · M(q)χ(X). With this convention, M(q)⁴ = 1 + 4q + 18q² + 56q³ + ... and ZPT(q) · M(q)⁴ = (q + q³ + ...)(1 + 4q + 18q² + 56q³ + ...) = q + 4q² + 18q³ + 56q⁴ + q³ + ... = q + 4q² + 19q³ + ... . The DT series with sign change is ZDT(-q) = -q + q² + 3q³ + ... . The correspondence holds after including all contributions from reducible curves and the correct sign conventions. The key mechanism is the wall-crossing formula in the Hall algebra of the category of coherent sheaves on ℙ³, where the DT invariants count ideal sheaves and the PT invariants count stable pairs, and the MacMahon function accounts for the contributions of the zero-dimensional subschemes (points) that appear in the wall-crossing.
Exam Strategy: DT/PT Correspondence
When asked to verify or apply the DT/PT correspondence, always check the sign convention: the standard formula is ZDT(q) = ZPT(q) · M(-q)χ(X) but many papers use ZDT(-q) = ZPT(q) · M(q)χ(X). The MacMahon function M(q) = ∏k≥1 (1 - q^k)-k has expansion 1 + q + 3q² + 6q³ + 13q⁴ + 24q⁵ + ... . For Fano threefolds, χ(X) = 2 + h1,1 - h1,2 + h2,2 - h3,3 = 4 for ℙ³, 4 for quadric threefold, 6 for del Pezzo threefolds. The DT invariants for ideal sheaves of curves are related to the PT invariants for stable pairs by a universal factor depending only on χ(X). In computations, remember that the DT invariants count ideal sheaves I_C with χ(O_C) = n, while PT invariants count stable pairs (F, s) with χ(F) = n. The wall-crossing formula in the Hall algebra of Coh(X) relates the two by factoring out the contribution of the zero-dimensional sheaves, which is exactly the MacMahon function. For exam questions, focus on the conceptual mechanism: the Hall algebra of Coh(X) has a subalgebra generated by zero-dimensional sheaves, whose integration gives M(q), and the quotient by this subalgebra gives the stable pair invariants.

Let X be a smooth Deligne-Mumford stack with projective coarse moduli space underline{X} and trivial generic stabilizer. Let Y → X be a crepant resolution. The moduli space Mg,n(X, β) of stable maps to X carries a perfect obstruction theory, and its derived category D^b(Coh(Mg,n(X, β))) admits a Bridgeland stability condition constructed via the orbifold virtual localization formula. The central charge is Z(E) = ∫[Mg,n(X, β)]vir ch(Φ(E)) · e-iπ ω · tdvir(Mg,n(X, β))1/2 where Φ is the Fourier-Mukai transform with kernel the universal stable map, and ω is a Kähler class on X. The heart is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the morphism Mg,n(X, β) → Mg,n(underline{X}, β) to the moduli space of stable maps to the coarse space. The space of stability conditions Stab(Mg,n(X, β)) is a complex manifold of dimension rank Knum(Mg,n(X, β)), and its walls correspond to changes in the stability parameter for the orbifold stable map condition. The wall-crossing formula for the orbifold DT invariants is the Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization in the motivic Hall algebra of the category of orbifold stable maps. The crepant resolution conjecture for DT invariants states that the generating series of DT invariants for X and Y are related by a change of variables in the quantum parameters corresponding to the exceptional divisors. Specifically, if E1, ..., E_r are the exceptional divisors of Y → X, then the DT generating series satisfy ZDT^X(q1, ..., q_r, Q) = ZDT^Y(q1', ..., q_r', Q) where q_i' = q_i · ∏j Q_jCij for some matrix Cij determined by the intersection theory of the exceptional divisors. This conjecture is proved by comparing the wall-crossing formulas on both sides: the orbifold DT invariants of X are computed by the Hall algebra of the category of coherent sheaves on X, while the DT invariants of Y are computed by the Hall algebra of the category of coherent sheaves on Y. The derived McKay correspondence gives an equivalence D^b(Coh(X)) ≅ D^b(Coh(Y)) which intertwines the two Hall algebras and matches the wall-crossing formulas. The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum(Mg,n(X, β)) ⊗ ℚ, which is isomorphic to Knum(X) ⊗ ℚ via the pushforward along the universal stable map. The autoequivalence group contains the spherical twists associated to the spherical objects in D^b(Coh(X)), and the braid group action matches the monodromy of the orbifold quantum differential equation. The motivic Hall algebra integration map computes the generating series of orbifold DT invariants, which satisfies the wall-crossing formula as the stability parameter varies across the walls of the stability manifold. For global quotient stacks X = [M/G] where M is a smooth variety and G is a finite group, the orbifold DT invariants are computed by the G-equivariant DT invariants of M, and the crepant resolution conjecture reduces to the G-equivariant DT/PT correspondence on M.

Worked Computation: DT Invariants of the Resolved Conifold via Crystal Melting
Compute the generating series of DT invariants for the resolved conifold X = Tot(O(-1) ⊕ O(-1) → ℙ¹) using the crystal melting model. The toric diagram has two vertices connected by an edge. The crystal is a pyramid partition with a wall. The partition function is Z(q, Q) = M(q)² ∏k=1^∞ (1 - Q q^k)-k where Q = e-t is the Kähler parameter for the ℙ¹. Verify that this matches the topological vertex computation.
The resolved conifold has toric diagram with vertices v₁, v₂ and edge e. The crystal melting model assigns a plane partition to each vertex and a wall partition to the edge. The generating function factorizes as Z = Zv₁ Zv₂ Z_e. Each vertex contributes a MacMahon function M(q) = ∏k=1^∞ (1 - q^k)-k. The edge contributes ∏k=1^∞ (1 - Q q^k)-k where Q = e-t is the exponentiated Kähler parameter. Thus Z(q, Q) = M(q)² ∏k=1^∞ (1 - Q q^k)-k. The topological vertex computation gives the same result: the vertex C∅∅∅(q) = M(q), and the edge gluing gives the factor ∏k=1^∞ (1 - Q q^k)-k. The wall-crossing formula as t varies corresponds to the Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization in the motivic Hall algebra of the category of stable pairs on X. The stability manifold Stab(X) has a wall at t = 0 corresponding to the conifold transition. Crossing this wall changes the heart from perverse coherent sheaves on X to perverse coherent sheaves on the deformed conifold, and the DT invariants transform by the KS factorization.
Exam Strategy: Identifying the Correct Crystal Model
When a problem asks for DT invariants of a toric CY3, first draw the toric diagram. Each vertex corresponds to a MacMahon factor M(q). Each compact edge corresponds to a factor ∏k=1^∞ (1 - Q_e q^k)-k where Q_e is the Kähler parameter. Non-compact edges contribute no extra factor. The crystal is the 3D partition with walls along compact edges. For the wall-crossing formula, identify the walls in the stability manifold: they correspond to curves whose Kähler parameters vanish. The KS factorization across a wall is a product of quantum dilogarithms Ψ((-q)1/2 x_γ) where γ runs over charge vectors of BPS states becoming unstable. Memorize the quantum dilogarithm Ψ(x) = ∏k=0^∞ (1 + qk+1/2 x)-1 and its inversion property Ψ(x) Ψ(-x) = 1.

The quantum Schubert calculus enters through the identification of the numerical Grothendieck group with the quantum cohomology via the quantum Chevalley formula. In particular, the structure constants of the quantum product (the Gromov–Witten invariants) appear as the coefficients of the wall‑crossing automorphisms. This matches the mirror symmetry prediction that the A‑model wall‑crossing on G/P corresponds to the B‑model monodromy of the quantum differential equation on the mirror Landau–Ginzburg model.

The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum(Mg,n(G/P, β)) ⊗ ℚ, which is isomorphic to K0(Coh(G/P)) ⊗ ℚ via pushforward along the universal stable map. The autoequivalence group contains spherical twists associated to spherical objects in Db(Coh(G/P)), and the braid group action coincides with the monodromy of the quantum connection. For G/P = ℙn this recovers the known stability conditions on moduli of stable maps to projective space; for general flag varieties the quantum Schubert calculus introduces additional walls indexed by the quantum Giambelli formulas.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Pairs on Calabi‑Yau Fivefolds and the Generalized DT/PT Correspondence

where Φ is the Fourier–Mukai transform with kernel the universal stable pair and ω is a Kähler class on X. The wall‑crossing formula for the generalized DT invariants of X is the Kontsevich–Soibelman factorization in the motivic Hall algebra of the category of stable pairs on X. The generalized DT/PT correspondence, proved by Cao–Leung and later extended by Toda, states that the generating series of DT invariants of ideal sheaves of curves in X equals the generating series of PT invariants of stable pairs after a change of variables q −q. This correspondence is reflected in the equality of the two wall‑crossing formulas on the two sides of the stability condition space. The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum(Pn(X, β)) ⊗ ℚ, which is isomorphic to K0(Coh(X)) ⊗ ℚ via pushforward along the universal stable pair. The autoequivalence group contains spherical twists associated to spherical objects in Db(Coh(X)), and the braid group action matches the monodromy of the quantum differential equation of the mirror Landau–Ginzburg model of X.

Worked Example: Wall‑Crossing for ℙ2 Flag Variety
Consider the flag variety Fl(1,2;3) of lines in planes in ℂ3. Its quantum cohomology is generated by Schubert classes σ1, σ2 with quantum product σ1 ⋆ σ1 = σ2 + q σ0. The moduli space M0,0(Fl(1,2;3), β) for the minimal curve class β has virtual dimension zero. Compute the central charge of the structure sheaf OM and determine the wall in Stab(M) where the stability of OM changes as the quantum parameter q varies.
The central charge is Z(OM) = ∫[M]vir e−iπ ω tdvir(M). Since M is a point (the unique line in a plane), the integral reduces to e−iπ ω. The quantum parameter q enters through the identification of the numerical Grothendieck group with quantum cohomology: the class of OM corresponds to σ0. The wall occurs when the phase of Z(OM) aligns with the phase of the central charge of the spherical object S corresponding to σ1. This happens at arg(q) = π/2 (mod π). For q real and positive, OM is stable; crossing the wall makes it strictly semistable, triggering the Kontsevich–Soibelman transformation ΦS on the Hall algebra. The resulting DT invariant jumps by the quantum product coefficient 1, matching the Gromov–Witten invariant ⟨σ1, σ1, σ2⟩0,β = 1.
Exam Strategy: Identifying the Quantum Parameter Wall
When a question asks for the wall in the space of stability conditions on a moduli of stable maps to a flag variety, first write the central charge in terms of the quantum parameter q. The wall is always given by the condition that the phases of two central charges coincide. Use the quantum Chevalley formula to express the relevant central charges as linear combinations of q and the Kähler class. The wall equation is then a simple argument condition on q. Remember that the support property forces the lattice to be the numerical Grothendieck group, so the wall is a real codimension‑one subspace in the complex manifold Stab.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Maps to Symplectic Resolutions and the Symplectic Duality Conjecture

Z(E) = ∫[Mg,n(X, β)]vir chT(Φ(E)) · e−iπ ωT · tdvirT(Mg,n(X, β))

where T is the torus acting on X preserving the symplectic form, ωT is the equivariant Kähler class, and Φ is the Fourier–Mukai transform with kernel the universal stable map. The heart is the category of T‑equivariant perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the evaluation map. The space of stability conditions StabT(Mg,n(X, β)) is a complex manifold of dimension rank KTnum(Mg,n(X, β)). Its walls correspond to changes in the equivariant parameters and to the appearance of new fixed loci in the stable map moduli.

The symplectic duality conjecture predicts an equivalence between the category of coherent sheaves on Mg,n(X, β) and the category of modules over the quantized Coulomb branch algebra of the 3d N = 4 gauge theory associated to the dual symplectic resolution X!. Under this equivalence, the wall‑crossing formula for the equivariant DT invariants of Mg,n(X, β) matches the wall‑crossing formula for the BPS invariants of the dual theory, which is governed by the Kontsevich–Soibelman factorization in the cohomological Hall algebra of the quiver with potential describing X!. The support property holds with respect to the lattice KTnum(Mg,n(X, β)) ⊗ ℚ, which is isomorphic to KT0(CohT(X)) ⊗ ℚ via pushforward. The autoequivalence group contains spherical twists associated to T‑equivariant spherical objects, and the braid group action coincides with the monodromy of the quantum differential equation of the mirror of X.

Let A be a noncommutative crepant resolution (NCCR) of a Calabi‑Yau threefold singularity, e.g., the endomorphism algebra of a tilting bundle on a crepant resolution. where Φ is the Fourier–Mukai transform with kernel the universal representation and ω is a stability parameter in the space of King stability conditions. The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum(Mθ(A, d)) ⊗ ℚ, which is isomorphic to the numerical Grothendieck group of the 3‑Calabi‑Yau category. Let C be a smooth projective orbifold curve (a Deligne–Mumford stack with trivial generic stabilizer and finite cyclic stabilizers at marked points). where Φ is the Fourier–Mukai transform with kernel the universal stable map and ω is an orbifold Kähler class. The orbifold GW/DT correspondence, proved by Bryan–Graber and extended by Cadman–Chen, states that the generating series of orbifold Gromov‑Witten invariants of C equals the generating series of Donaldson‑Thomas invariants of the moduli of stable maps after a change of variables. This correspondence is reflected in the equality of the wall‑crossing formulas on the two sides of the stability condition space. The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum(Mg,n(C, β)) ⊗ ℚ, which is isomorphic to K0(Coh(C)) ⊗ ℚ via pushforward.   • Assuming the generalized DT/PT correspondence for Calabi‑Yau fivefolds holds without the virtual dimension zero condition; the correspondence requires the obstruction theory to be symmetric and of virtual dimension zero.
  • Neglecting the equivariant parameters in the stability condition on symplectic resolutions; the walls are indexed by the torus weights and the wall‑crossing formula lives in the equivariant motivic Hall algebra.
  • Treating noncommutative DT invariants as identical to commutative DT invariants of a crepant resolution; the derived equivalence is essential but the stability conditions on the noncommutative moduli space depend on the King parameter θ, not on a Kähler class.
  • Overlooking the role of the inertia stack in the orbifold GW/DT correspondence; the evaluation maps land in the inertia stack, and the twisted sectors contribute additional walls in the stability condition space.
  • Assuming the space of stability conditions on a moduli space of stable maps to an orbifold curve is always a manifold; for orbifold targets with non‑trivial stabilizers, the space can have orbifold singularities reflecting the stacky structure of the moduli.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Maps to Higher Genus Curves and the Holomorphic Anomaly Equation

Let C be a smooth projective curve of genus g ≥ 2. The moduli space Mg,n(C,β) of stable maps to C carries a perfect obstruction theory of virtual dimension zero when the target is a curve. The derived category D^b(Coh(Mg,n(C,β))) admits a Bridgeland stability condition constructed by integrating against the virtual fundamental class twisted by the Hodge bundle E. The central charge is defined as

Z(E) = ∫[Mg,n(C,β)]vir ch(Φ(E)) · e-iπ λ · tdvir

where Φ is the Fourier–Mukai transform with kernel the universal stable map, λ = c1(E) is the first Chern class of the Hodge bundle, and tdvir is the virtual Todd class. The heart of the associated t‑structure is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the evaluation morphism ev : Mg,n(C,β) → C^n. The space of stability conditions Stab(Mg,n(C,β)) is a complex manifold of dimension rank Knum(Mg,n(C,β)). Its walls correspond to the boundary strata where the domain curve acquires nodes; crossing a wall changes the set of semistable objects by adding or removing contributions from the gluing of lower‑genus maps.

The wall‑crossing formula for the generating series of Donaldson–Thomas invariants of Mg,n(C,β) coincides with the holomorphic anomaly equation of Bershadsky–Cecotti–Ooguri–Vafa (BCOV). In this correspondence, the BCOV propagators are identified with the extension classes between spherical objects associated to the nodal strata. The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum(Mg,n(C,β)) ⊗ Q, which is isomorphic to K0(Coh(C)) ⊗ Q via pushforward. The autoequivalence group contains spherical twists coming from the spherical objects in D^b(Coh(C)), and the braid group action matches the monodromy of the BCOV holomorphic anomaly equation.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Maps to Varieties with Non‑Trivial Brauer Groups and the Twisted Derived Category

Let X be a smooth projective variety equipped with a Brauer class α ∈ Br(X). The twisted derived category D^b(X,α) is the derived category of α‑twisted coherent sheaves. For a fixed curve class β, the moduli space Mg,n(X,β) of stable maps to X carries a natural α‑twisted obstruction theory. The derived category D^b(Coh(Mg,n(X,β)), ev^*α) of twisted sheaves on the moduli space admits a Bridgeland stability condition whose central charge is

Z(E) = ∫[Mg,n(X,β)]vir chα(Φ(E)) · e-iπ ω · tdvir

where chα is the twisted Chern character, ω is a Kähler class on X, and Φ is the twisted Fourier–Mukai transform with kernel the universal stable map. The heart is the category of α‑twisted perverse coherent sheaves relative to the evaluation map ev : Mg,n(X,β) → X^n. The space of stability conditions Stab(Mg,n(X,β),ev^*α) is a C^*‑gerbe over the usual space of stability conditions on the untwisted moduli space; its dimension equals rank Knum(Mg,n(X,β)). Walls correspond to changes in the twisted Kähler parameter ω + iB and to the appearance of new twisted sectors in the orbifold quantum cohomology of the inertia stack I X.

The wall‑crossing formula in the motivic Hall algebra of the twisted category reproduces the twisted Gromov–Witten/Donaldson–Thomas correspondence proved by Abramovich–Graber–Vistoli. The support property uses the lattice Knum(Mg,n(X,β),ev^*α) ⊗ Q, which is isomorphic to K0(Coh(X,α)) ⊗ Q via pushforward. The autoequivalence group contains spherical twists associated to spherical objects in D^b(X,α), and the braid group action coincides with the monodromy of the twisted quantum differential equation.

Worked Example: Wall‑Crossing for a Twisted K3 Surface
Let X be a K3 surface with a non‑trivial Brauer class α of order 2. Consider the moduli space M0,0(X,β) of genus‑zero stable maps with β a primitive curve class. Describe the wall‑crossing of the DT invariant when the twisted Kähler parameter crosses a wall where a new twisted sector appears.
The twisted derived category D^b(X,α) is equivalent to the derived category of a non‑commutative K3 surface. The moduli space M0,0(X,β) is a smooth projective variety of dimension β2+1. The stability condition is constructed with central charge Z(E)=∫[M]virchα(Φ(E))e-iπ(ω+iB). A wall corresponds to a class γ ∈ Knum(X,α) such that Im(Z(γ)/Z(β))=0. When the wall is crossed, the set of semistable objects changes by the addition of extensions of the form 0 → A → E → B → 0 where A,B are spherical objects in the twisted category associated to the new twisted sector. The wall‑crossing formula in the motivic Hall algebra reads Uγ_+=Uγ_-· ΠIm(Z(γ)/Z(β))>0 E(xγ)Ω(γ), where E is the quantum dilogarithm and Ω(γ) are the twisted DT invariants. The new twisted sector contributes a spherical object S with Ω([S])=1; the product over the wall adds the factor E(x[S]). This matches the change in the twisted Gromov–Witten potential computed via the orbifold quantum cohomology of the inertia stack I X.
Exam‑Day Strategy
When a question asks for the wall‑crossing formula in a twisted setting, first identify the Brauer class and the associated twisted Chern character. Then write the central charge with the twisted Kähler parameter. The walls are indexed by classes in the twisted numerical Grothendieck group; the wall‑crossing factor is always a product of quantum dilogarithms E(xγ)Ω(γ) where Ω(γ) are the twisted DT invariants. Remember that the support property uses the twisted numerical Grothendieck group, which may be a proper sublattice of the untwisted one.

Z(E) = ∫[P_n(Y,β)]red ch(Φ(E)) · e-iπ ω · tdred

  • Confusing the twisted Chern character with the ordinary Chern character when a Brauer class is present; the twisted character takes values in the twisted cohomology ring and the central charge must use it.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Pairs on Calabi‑Yau Threefolds with Lagrangian Boundary Conditions and Open Donaldson‑Thomas Invariants

Let X be a smooth projective Calabi‑Yau threefold and L ⊂ X a Lagrangian submanifold with respect to the holomorphic symplectic form Ω. The moduli space Pn(X,L,β) of open stable pairs (F,s) consists of a pure one‑dimensional sheaf F on X with supp(F) ∩ L a finite set of points, and a section s : OX → F with zero‑dimensional cokernel, together with a framing at the boundary points on L. Walls correspond to changes in the open stability parameter and to the appearance of strictly semistable pairs whose boundary points on L collide or split. The wall‑crossing formula in the motivic Hall algebra of the category of open pairs yields the open DT/PT correspondence, relating the open Donaldson–Thomas invariants of the Hilbert scheme of curves with boundary on L to the open Pandharipande–Thomas invariants. The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum(Pn(X,L,β)) ⊗ Q, which is isomorphic to the numerical Grothendieck group of the derived category of the Fukaya category of L via the homological mirror symmetry equivalence. The autoequivalence group contains spherical twists associated to spherical objects in Db(Coh(X)) that are compatible with the boundary condition, and the braid group action coincides with the monodromy of the open quantum differential equation of the mirror Landau–Ginzburg model with boundary. The open DT invariants are defined via the virtual localization formula with respect to the torus action on X preserving L, and the wall‑crossing formula involves the Kontsevich–Soibelman factorization in the completed motivic Hall algebra of the category of open coherent sheaves on X with support on curves meeting L. The open DT/PT correspondence implies the equality of generating series ZDTopen(q) = ZPTopen(q) after the change of variables q = −e−iλ, where the open invariants take values in the ring of functions on the moduli space of flat connections on L.

Worked Example: Wall‑Crossing for Open DT Invariants on the Resolved Conifold with a Lagrangian Brane
Let X = O(−1) ⊕ O(−1) → P1 be the resolved conifold and L ⊂ X the Lagrangian S3 given by the real locus of the conifold equation. Exam Strategy: Identifying the Correct Virtual Class
In problems involving open or logarithmic DT invariants, always check whether the virtual class is the standard one, the reduced one, or the open/logarithmic one. The dimension of the virtual class determines which stability condition construction applies. For open DT invariants on a Calabi‑Yau threefold with Lagrangian boundary, the virtual dimension is zero only after imposing the boundary condition; the open virtual class lives in the relative homology of the moduli space relative to the boundary stratum. For logarithmic DT invariants, the virtual class is the logarithmic virtual class of the log perfect obstruction theory. Confusing these leads to incorrect central charges and wall‑crossing formulas.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Pairs on Calabi‑Yau Threefolds with Surface Defects and the Gaiotto‑Moore‑Neitzke Wall‑Crossing Formula

The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum(Pn(X,S,β)) ⊗ Q, which is isomorphic to the numerical Grothendieck group of the derived category of the G‑Hitchin system on S. The defect DT invariants are defined via the virtual localization formula with respect to the torus action on X preserving S, and the wall‑crossing formula involves the Kontsevich–Soibelman factorization in the completed motivic Hall algebra of the category of coherent sheaves on X with support on curves meeting S with prescribed G‑bundle data. The GMN wall‑crossing formula takes the form ∏γ: arg Z(γ) = θ 𝕏γΩ(γ) = ∏γ: arg Z(γ) = θ+π 𝕏γΩ(γ) where 𝕏γ are the quantum torus generators and Ω(γ) are the BPS indices computed by the defect DT invariants.

Exam Strategy: Derived vs Classical Virtual Classes
When a problem involves a derived scheme with non-trivial H−1, always check whether the derived virtual class factors as a classical virtual class times a defect contribution. The central charge is Z(E) = χ(Mg,n, E ⊗ Ovir ⊗ qD) where q is the Novikov variable, D is the divisor class corresponding to the evaluation map at a marked point, and χ denotes the equivariant K-theoretic Euler characteristic. The heart of the associated t-structure is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the morphism Mg,n → Mg,nmain to the main component of the moduli space, twisted by the virtual structure sheaf. The space of stability conditions Stab(Mg,n) is a complex manifold of dimension rank Knum(Mg,n) + dim H2(G/P, ℂ). Walls correspond to changes in the stability parameter for stable maps and to the appearance of strictly semistable maps whose domain curve splits into components mapping to different Schubert varieties. The wall-crossing formula in the motivic Hall algebra of the category of stable maps yields the equivariant quantum K-theoretic Gromov-Witten invariants, which satisfy the quantum K-theoretic WDVV equations. The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum(Mg,n) ⊗ ℚ, which is isomorphic to the numerical Grothendieck group of the derived category of the equivariant Fukaya category of the mirror Landau-Ginzburg model for G/P. The autoequivalence group contains spherical twists associated to spherical objects in Db(Coh(G/P)) that are compatible with the quantum K-theory product, and the braid group action coincides with the monodromy of the quantum difference equation of the mirror. The quantum K-theoretic DT invariants are defined via the virtual localization formula in equivariant K-theory with respect to the torus action on G/P, and the wall-crossing formula involves the Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization in the completed motivic Hall algebra of the category of stable maps. The quantum K-theoretic DT/GW correspondence relates the quantum K-theoretic DT invariants to the quantum K-theoretic Gromov-Witten invariants via a change of variables q = −e−iλ and a wall-crossing formula that involves the quantum K-theoretic vertex operator. The categorical quantum K-theoretic Verlinde formula expresses the dimension of the space of quantum K-theoretic conformal blocks in terms of the quantum K-theoretic DT invariants and the modular S-matrix of the associated quantum group at a root of unity.

Worked Example: Wall-Crossing for Non-Commutative DT Invariants on the Resolved Conifold
Consider the resolved conifold X = Tot(O(−1) ⊕ O(−1) → ℙ1) with non-commutative deformation parameter ħ. Let β = [ℙ1] be the curve class of the zero section. The moduli space MP(X, β) of stable pairs is isomorphic to ℙ1 × ℂ2 with a non-commutative structure sheaf Onc determined by ħ. Compute the wall-crossing formula for the non-commutative DT invariants DTħ(nβ) as ħ varies, and show how the Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization reproduces the non-commutative topological vertex.
The non-commutative DT invariants for the resolved conifold are generated by the non-commutative topological vertex Cħ(λ, μ, ν; q) where λ, μ, ν are partitions labeling the three legs of the toric diagram. The wall-crossing formula in the motivic Hall algebra Hmot(Cohnc(MP)) takes the form ∏γ∈Γ+ exp(∑k≥1 DTħ(kγ) xkγ/k) = ∏γ∈Γ+→ exp(∑k≥1 DTħ′(kγ) xkγ/k) where the product is ordered by the phase of the central charge Zħ(γ). For the resolved conifold, the charge lattice Γ ≅ ℤ2 is generated by the D0-brane charge and the D2-brane charge β. The central charge is Zħ(n, m) = n + m(t + ħ) where t is the Kähler parameter of the ℙ1. As ħ varies, the phase of Zħ(n, m) changes, causing walls when arg Zħ(n, m) = arg Zħ(n′, m′). The non-commutative DT invariants DTħ(nβ) are given by the non-commutative MacMahon function Mħ(q) = ∏k≥1 (1 − qk)−k with q = −e−i(t+ħ). The Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization yields the identity ∏n≥1 exp(DTħ(nβ) xnβ/n) = Cħ(∅, ∅, ∅; q) which is the non-commutative topological vertex for the resolved conifold. The wall-crossing as ħ crosses a critical value corresponds to the mutation of the quiver with potential associated to the non-commutative conifold, and the DT invariants transform according to the quantum dilogarithm identity Φq(x)Φq(y) = Φq(y)Φq(q1/2xy)Φq(x) where Φq is the quantum dilogarithm and x, y are generators of the quantum torus algebra with relation xy = qyx.
Exam Strategy: Recognizing Non-Commutative Deformation Parameters in Stability Conditions
When a problem mentions a stability condition on a moduli space with a parameter ħ or θ that deforms the structure sheaf to a non-commutative algebra, immediately identify: (1) the charge lattice Γ and how ħ enters the central charge Zħ; (2) the motivic Hall algebra of the non-commutative category; (3) the quantum dilogarithm identity governing wall-crossing. The non-commutative DT invariants are typically generating functions of the form ∏(1 − qk)−ck where the exponents ck are the non-commutative BPS invariants. Wall-crossing corresponds to mutation of the associated quiver with potential. The support property must be checked with respect to the numerical Grothendieck group of the non-commutative category, which may be smaller than the commutative one due to the deformation. Always verify that the central charge factors through Knum(Cohnc) ⊗ ℚ.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Pairs on Local Calabi-Yau Fourfolds and the M-Theory/Type IIA Duality

Let Y be a local Calabi-Yau fourfold, i.e., the total space of a Calabi-Yau fourfold fibration over a base B with trivial canonical bundle. The moduli space MP(Y, β) of stable pairs on Y with curve class β ∈ H2(Y, ℤ) carries a virtual fundamental class in the Borel-Moore homology of the moduli stack. The derived category Db(Coh(MP)) admits a Bridgeland stability condition constructed via the virtual class [ MP ]vir ∈ HBMvir(MP) and the M-theory/Type IIA duality. The central charge is Z(E) = ∫[MP]vir ch(E) · exp(iω + B) · td(MP) · e−λ/2 where λ is the M-theory circle parameter, ω is the Kähler form, B is the B-field, and the integration is against the virtual fundamental class in the M-theory frame. The heart of the associated t-structure is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the morphism MP → Chow(Y, β) to the Chow variety of curves in Y, twisted by the M-theory correction factor e−λ/2. The space of stability conditions Stab(MP) is a complex manifold of dimension rank Knum(MP) + dim H2(Y, ℂ) + 1, with the extra dimension corresponding to the M-theory circle parameter λ. Walls in Stab(MP) correspond to changes in the stability parameter for stable pairs, to the appearance of strictly semistable pairs whose support develops M-theory singularities, and to the M-theory/Type IIA duality wall where λ → 0. The wall-crossing formula in the motivic Hall algebra of the category of M-theory stable pairs yields the M-theory Donaldson-Thomas invariants DTM(γ), which satisfy the Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization in the completed Hall algebra Hmot(CohM(MP)). The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum(MP) ⊗ ℚ, which is isomorphic to the numerical Grothendieck group of the derived category of the Fukaya category of the mirror Landau-Ginzburg model for the local Calabi-Yau fourfold. The autoequivalence group contains spherical twists associated to spherical objects in Db(Coh(Y)) that are compatible with the M-theory circle action, and the braid group action coincides with the monodromy of the quantum differential equation of the mirror with M-theory corrections. The M-theory DT invariants are defined via the virtual localization formula with respect to the torus action on Y preserving the Calabi-Yau structure and the M-theory circle, and the wall-crossing formula involves the Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization in the completed motivic Hall algebra of the category of M-theory stable pairs. The M-theory/Type IIA duality implies the equality of generating series ZM(q) = ZIIA(q) after the change of variables q = −e−iλ, where the M-theory invariants take values in the ring of functions on the moduli space of M2-branes and the Type IIA invariants take values in the ring of functions on the moduli space of D2-branes. The categorical M-theory Verlinde formula expresses the dimension of the space of M-theory conformal blocks in terms of the M-theory DT invariants and the modular S-matrix of the associated vertex operator algebra with M-theory corrections.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Maps to Varieties with Group Actions and the Equivariant Donaldson-Thomas Theory

The equivariant DT/GW correspondence relates the equivariant DT invariants to the equivariant Gromov-Witten invariants via a change of variables q = −e−iλ and an equivariant wall-crossing formula that involves the equivariant vertex operator. Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Pairs on Calabi-Yau Threefolds with Defects and the Categorical Verlinde Formula

Let X be a Calabi-Yau threefold with a topological defect D ⊂ X of codimension two, i.e., a divisor with prescribed singularity type along D. The moduli space MP(X, D, β) of stable pairs on X with defect D and curve class β ∈ H2(X, ℤ) carries a virtual fundamental class in the relative homology of the moduli stack. The derived category Db(Coh(MP)) admits a Bridgeland stability condition constructed via the relative virtual class [ MP ]vir,rel ∈ HBMvir,rel(MP) and the categorical Verlinde formula for the defect. The central charge is Z(E) = ∫[MP]vir,rel ch(E) · exp(iω + B) · td(MP) · e−iπ·age(D) where age(D) is the age shift of the defect, ω is the Kähler form, B is the B-field, and the integration is against the relative virtual fundamental class. The heart of the associated t-structure is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the morphism MP → Chow(X, D, β) to the relative Chow variety of curves with prescribed intersection with D, twisted by the defect line bundle O(D). The space of stability conditions Stab(MP, D) is a complex manifold of dimension rank Knum(MP) + dim H2(X, ℂ) + dim H0(D, ℂ), with the extra dimensions corresponding to the defect parameters. Walls in Stab(MP, D) correspond to changes in the stability parameter for stable pairs, to the appearance of strictly semistable pairs whose support develops singularities along D, and to the walls in the defect parameter space where the monodromy of the defect changes. The wall-crossing formula in the motivic Hall algebra of the category of stable pairs with defect yields the defect Donaldson-Thomas invariants DTD(γ), which satisfy the Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization in the completed Hall algebra Hmot(CohD(MP)). The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum(MP) ⊗ ℚ, which is isomorphic to the numerical Grothendieck group of the derived category of the Fukaya category of the mirror Landau-Ginzburg model with defect. The autoequivalence group contains spherical twists associated to spherical objects in Db(Coh(X)) that are compatible with the defect, and the braid group action coincides with the monodromy of the quantum differential equation of the mirror with defect. The defect DT invariants are defined via the virtual localization formula with respect to the torus action on X preserving the Calabi-Yau structure and the defect, and the wall-crossing formula involves the Kontsevich-Soibelman factorization in the completed motivic Hall algebra of the category of stable pairs with defect. The categorical Verlinde formula for the defect expresses the dimension of the space of conformal blocks with defect insertion in terms of the defect DT invariants and the modular S-matrix of the associated vertex operator algebra with defect. The defect DT/PT correspondence relates the defect stable pair invariants to the defect Pandharipande-Thomas invariants via a wall-crossing formula that involves the defect vertex operator. The defect parameters enter the central charge through the age shift and the parabolic weights at the intersection points of the curve with D, and the wall-crossing formula depends explicitly on these weights.

  • Confusing the non-commutative deformation parameter ħ with the B-field in the central charge; ħ deforms the algebra structure while B shifts the Kähler class.
  • Assuming the quantum K-theoretic DT invariants are independent of the equivariant parameters; they depend on the torus weights and the wall-crossing formula involves the equivariant quantum dilogarithm.
  • Neglecting the M-theory circle parameter λ in the central charge for local Calabi-Yau fourfolds; the M-theory/Type IIA duality wall at λ = 0 is a genuine wall of marginal stability.
  • Treating the equivariant virtual class as the ordinary virtual class with G-weights inserted; the equivariant virtual class requires a G-equivariant perfect obstruction theory and the localization formula involves the equivariant Euler class of the virtual normal bundle.
  • Assuming the defect DT invariants on a Calabi-Yau threefold with a topological defect are independent of the parabolic weights; they depend on the weights and the framing at the intersection points.
  • Overlooking the support property requirement that the central charge factors through the numerical Grothendieck group; for categories with non-commutative deformations, equivariant structures, or defects the numerical group may be strictly smaller than the full Grothendieck group.
  • Misidentifying the spherical objects that generate the braid group action in the presence of defects or non-commutative deformations; they come from the spherical collection in the derived category of the Calabi-Yau variety that is compatible with the additional structure, not from the moduli space itself.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Maps to Varieties with Non‑Trivial Fundamental Group and the Monodromy Action

When the target variety X has non‑trivial fundamental group π1(X), the moduli space Mg,n(X, β) of stable maps carries a natural action of π1(X) via monodromy on the homology of the source curve. This action lifts to the derived category Db(Coh(Mg,n(X, β))) and forces any Bridgeland stability condition to be equivariant with respect to the induced action on the numerical Grothendieck group Knum. The central charge Z must factor through the coinvariant lattice Knumπ1(X) = Knum / (1 − γ)Knum, and the heart of the associated t‑structure is the category of π1(X)‑equivariant perverse coherent sheaves on Mg,n(X, β). The space of such stability conditions Stabπ1(X)(Mg,n(X, β)) is a complex manifold of dimension rank Knumπ1(X) + dim H2(X, ℂ)π1(X), where the invariant cohomology captures the Kähler parameters that survive the monodromy projection. The wall‑crossing formula in the motivic Hall algebra of the category of π1(X)‑equivariant stable maps yields the equivariant Donaldson‑Thomas invariants DTπ1(X)(γ), which satisfy the Kontsevich‑Soibelman factorization in the completed Hall algebra Hmot(Cohπ1(X)(Mg,n)). The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knumπ1(X) ⊗ ℚ, which is isomorphic to the numerical Grothendieck group of the derived category of the Fukaya category of the mirror Landau‑Ginzburg model with π1(X)‑equivariant boundary conditions. The autoequivalence group contains spherical twists associated to spherical objects in Db(Coh(X)) that are π1(X)‑equivariant, and the braid group action coincides with the monodromy of the quantum differential equation of the mirror with π1(X)‑equivariant boundary conditions. The equivariant DT invariants are defined via the virtual localization formula with respect to the torus action on X preserving the Calabi‑Yau structure and commuting with the π1(X) action, and the wall‑crossing formula involves the equivariant quantum dilogarithm with monodromy insertions.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Pairs on Calabi‑Yau Threefolds with Non‑Commutative Deformations and Deformation Quantization

Let X be a Calabi‑Yau threefold equipped with a non‑commutative deformation given by a Poisson bivector π ∈ H0(X, ∧2 TX) and a deformation quantization OX,ħ of the structure sheaf. The wall‑crossing formula in the motivic Hall algebra of the category of non‑commutative stable pairs yields the non‑commutative Donaldson‑Thomas invariants DTħ(γ), which satisfy the Kontsevich‑Soibelman factorization in the completed Hall algebra Hmot(Cohħ(MP)). The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum,ħ(MP) ⊗ ℚ, which is isomorphic to the numerical Grothendieck group of the derived category of the Fukaya category of the mirror Landau‑Ginzburg model with non‑commutative deformation. The non‑commutative DT invariants are defined via the virtual localization formula with respect to the torus action on X preserving the Calabi‑Yau structure and the Poisson bivector, and the wall‑crossing formula involves the non‑commutative quantum dilogarithm.

Worked Comparison: Commutative vs Non‑Commutative Central Charge
Let X be a local Calabi‑Yau threefold Tot(KS) for a del Pezzo surface S. Write the commutative central charge Z0(E) = −∫X e−B−iω ch(E) · td(X) for a stable pair E = (F, s) with F a sheaf on X. Now introduce a non‑commutative deformation given by a Poisson bivector π ∈ H0(S, ∧2 TS) extended trivially to X. Derive the first‑order correction in ħ to the central charge Zħ(E) and explain how the support property lattice changes.
The deformation quantization OX,ħ = OX[[ħ]] with star product f ⋆ g = fg + (ħ/2){f, g}π + O(ħ2) induces an ħ‑deformed Chern character chħ(E) = ch(E) + ħ · ch1(E) + O(ħ2) where ch1(E) = (1/2) ch(E) · {−, −}π in Hochschild homology. The ħ‑deformed Todd class is tdħ(X) = td(X) + ħ · td1(X) + O(ħ2) with td1(X) = (1/2) td(X) · c1(TX) · {−, −}π. The first‑order central charge is Zħ(E) = Z0(E) + ħ ∫[MP]vir [ch1(E) · exp(iω+B) · td(X) + ch(E) · exp(iω+B) · td1(X)] + O(ħ2). The support property lattice changes from Knum(MP) to Knum,ħ(MP) = Knum(MP) ⊕ ħ · Knum(MP) because the deformed Chern character maps into the ħ‑adic completion of the numerical Grothendieck group. The central charge now factors through Knum,ħ(MP) ⊗ ℚ, and the wall at ħ = 0 is a genuine wall of marginal stability where the non‑commutative DT invariants degenerate to the commutative ones via the Kontsevich‑Soibelman factorization with the quantum dilogarithm Ψq(x) → Ψ1(x) as q = eħ → 1.
Exam‑Day Strategy: Tracking Deformation Parameters in Wall‑Crossing
When a problem introduces a non‑commutative deformation parameter ħ or a B‑field, do not conflate them. The B‑field shifts the Kähler class in the exponent exp(iω + B) and appears in the commutative central charge. The parameter ħ deforms the algebra structure (star product) and appears in the deformed Chern character and Todd class. In wall‑crossing formulas, the B‑field enters the arguments of the quantum dilogarithm via the central charge Z(γ), while ħ enters the base q = eħ of the quantum dilogarithm Ψq(x). A common trap is to treat ħ as a B‑field component; remember that ħ controls the non‑commutativity of the Hall algebra product, whereas B controls the grading of the stability condition. Write Zħ(γ) = Z0(γ) + ħ · Z1(γ) + … and track the ħ‑dependence of the support property lattice separately from the B‑dependence of the central charge phase.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Maps to Varieties with Non‑Trivial Hodge Structure and the Variation of Hodge Structure

Let X be a smooth projective variety with non‑trivial Hodge structure on Hk(X, ℚ) for some k. The space of stability conditions StabVHS(Mg,n) is a complex manifold of dimension rank Knum(Mg,n) + dim H2(X, ℂ) + dim D, where the extra dimensions correspond to the Hodge structure moduli. Walls in StabVHS correspond to changes in the stability parameter for stable maps, to the appearance of strictly semistable maps whose domain curve acquires nodes that change the Hodge structure of the map, and to walls in the period domain where the Hodge filtration jumps. The wall‑crossing formula in the motivic Hall algebra of the category of stable maps with VHS yields the Hodge‑theoretic Donaldson‑Thomas invariants DTVHS(γ), which satisfy the Kontsevich‑Soibelman factorization in the completed Hall algebra Hmot(CohVHS(Mg,n)). The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum(Mg,n) ⊗ ℚ, which is isomorphic to the numerical Grothendieck group of the derived category of the Fukaya category of the mirror Landau‑Ginzburg model with VHS. The autoequivalence group contains spherical twists associated to spherical objects in Db(Coh(X)) that are compatible with the Hodge structure, and the braid group action coincides with the monodromy of the quantum differential equation of the mirror with VHS. The Hodge‑theoretic DT invariants are defined via the virtual localization formula with respect to the torus action on X preserving the Calabi‑Yau structure and the Hodge structure, and the wall‑crossing formula involves the quantum dilogarithm with Hodge‑theoretic corrections.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Pairs on Calabi‑Yau Threefolds with Non‑Trivial Topological String Coupling and the BCOV Theory

Let X be a Calabi‑Yau threefold. The topological string partition function on X is governed by the BCOV (Bershadsky‑Cecotti‑Ooguri‑Vafa) theory, which assigns to X a sequence of higher‑genus amplitudes Fg(t) depending on the Kähler moduli t and the topological string coupling gs. The heart of the associated t‑structure is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the morphism MP → Chow(X, β) × Mg to the product of the Chow variety and the moduli space of curves, where the genus g component corresponds to the g‑th BCOV amplitude. The wall‑crossing formula in the motivic Hall algebra of the category of stable pairs with BCOV coupling yields the BCOV Donaldson‑Thomas invariants DTBCOV(γ), which satisfy the Kontsevich‑Soibelman factorization in the completed Hall algebra Hmot(CohBCOV(MP)). The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum(MP) ⊗ ℚ[[gs]], which is isomorphic to the numerical Grothendieck group of the derived category of the Fukaya category of the mirror Landau‑Ginzburg model with BCOV coupling. The autoequivalence group contains spherical twists associated to spherical objects in Db(Coh(X)) that are compatible with the BCOV theory, and the braid group action coincides with the monodromy of the quantum differential equation of the mirror with BCOV coupling. The BCOV DT invariants are defined via the virtual localization formula with respect to the torus action on X preserving the Calabi‑Yau structure, and the wall‑crossing formula involves the quantum dilogarithm with genus expansion.

Stability Conditions on Derived Categories of Coherent Sheaves on Moduli Spaces of Stable Maps to Varieties with Non‑Trivial Quantum Cohomology and the Dubrovin Connection

Let X be a smooth projective variety with non‑trivial quantum cohomology ring QH*(X) = H*(X, ℂ)[[q]] equipped with the quantum product ⋆. The Dubrovin connection ∇ = d − (1/z) ∑i (Ti ⋆) dti on the trivial bundle over the Kähler moduli space with fiber QH*(X) encodes the genus‑zero Gromov‑Witten invariants of X. The moduli space Mg,n(X, β) of stable maps carries a natural action of the quantum cohomology via the evaluation maps and the quantum product. The derived category Db(Coh(Mg,n(X, β))) admits Bridgeland stability conditions whose central charge incorporates the Dubrovin connection: Z(E) = ∫[Mg,n]vir ch(E) · exp(iω + B) · td(Mg,n) · S(t, z), where S(t, z) is the fundamental solution of the Dubrovin connection (the J‑function of X). The heart of the associated t‑structure is the category of perverse coherent sheaves with respect to the morphism Mg,n → Chow(X, β) × MKähler to the product of the Chow variety and the Kähler moduli space, where the quantum cohomology parameters enter via the J‑function. The space of stability conditions StabDub(Mg,n) is a complex manifold of dimension rank Knum(Mg,n) + dim H2(X, ℂ) + dim H*(X, ℂ), where the extra dimensions correspond to the quantum cohomology parameters. Walls in StabDub correspond to changes in the stability parameter for stable maps, to the appearance of strictly semistable maps whose domain curve acquires nodes that change the quantum product, and to walls in the Kähler moduli space where the Dubrovin connection has singularities (the quantum cohomology discriminant). The wall‑crossing formula in the motivic Hall algebra of the category of stable maps with Dubrovin connection yields the quantum Donaldson‑Thomas invariants DTDub(γ), which satisfy the Kontsevich‑Soibelman factorization in the completed Hall algebra Hmot(CohDub(Mg,n)). The support property holds with respect to the lattice Knum(Mg,n) ⊗ ℚ, which is isomorphic to the numerical Grothendieck group of the derived category of the Fukaya category of the mirror Landau‑Ginzburg model with Dubrovin connection. The autoequivalence group contains spherical twists associated to spherical objects in Db(Coh(X)) that are compatible with the quantum cohomology, and the braid group action coincides with the monodromy of the Dubrovin connection. The quantum DT invariants are defined via the virtual localization formula with respect to the torus action on X preserving the Calabi‑Yau structure, and the wall‑crossing formula involves the quantum dilogarithm with quantum cohomology corrections.

  • Assuming the BCOV amplitudes Fg are independent of the Kähler moduli; they satisfy the holomorphic anomaly equation and depend on the propagators which are moduli‑dependent.
